name: Fobos-Grunt 2, Boomerang and Mars-Grunt
short_status: Paper only, and dormant with no announced end as of 27 August 2026: Boomerang reached technical proposals in 2019 and stopped there for want of money. No hardware was built and no cancellation was ever announced.

facts.label: Status on 27 August 2026
facts.value: Dormant with no announced end. We found no Roscosmos, Lavochkin or IKI statement dated 2024, 2025 or 2026 giving Boomerang a launch date, a design phase or a budget. The most recent schedule statement we could trace is from September 2023 and says only that launch would be after 2030. Russian Wikipedia's own article carries a banner flagging its contents as current as of October 2016.

facts.label: Three names, one project
facts.value: Фобос-Грунт 2 is the informal successor name used from January 2012. Бумеранг (Boomerang) is the spacecraft name that replaced it. Экспедиция-М (Expedition-M) is the state development work, the ОКР, inside which it sat. Alexander Zakharov of IKI, who worked on Phobos 1, Phobos 2 and Phobos-Grunt, told N+1 in February 2020 that Expedition-M contained two missions: one to Phobos with sample return, called Boomerang, and a second to Mars, also with sample return. TASS in 2015 instead printed the development work as Экспедиция-М (Марс-Грунт), which is why English sources sometimes treat Mars-Grunt and Expedition-M as the same thing.

facts.label: Where it came from
facts.value: Phobos-Grunt reached low Earth orbit on 8 November 2011 UTC, never fired for Mars, and re-entered on 15 January 2012. Work on a Fobos-Grunt 2 began at NPO Lavochkin with the Russian Academy of Sciences almost immediately. Speaking at the Korolev Readings at Bauman Moscow State Technical University on 24 January 2012, Lavochkin's general director Viktor Khartov said the task of returning soil from Phobos remained current, Russian scientists believed no other international programme would solve it within ten years, and "У нас нет другого пути: Россия должна решить задачу полёта на Марс" ("We have no other road: Russia must solve the task of the flight to Mars").

facts.label: What would have been different
facts.value: NTV reported on 23 January 2012 that IKI director Lev Zelyony said the project would be updated but simplified, with some of the Mars-observing instruments moved onto ESA's ExoMars if an agreement could be reached, and made the point that Phobos-Grunt had four tasks (fly to Mars, land on Phobos, launch back to Earth, deliver the return capsule) and that not one of them had ever been rehearsed. Russian Wikipedia records the intended engineering changes: a substantially revised service module with an improved control system, roughly six years of rework, fewer instruments, systems proved first on the Luna-Glob and Luna-Resurs missions, and a full Fregat upper stage instead of the truncated version widely blamed for 2011.

facts.label: Not started in 2013
facts.value: Asked at the MAKS-2013 air show whether work on a new Phobos mission had begun, Khartov answered plainly on 27 August 2013, in reply to a RIA Novosti question: "Нет, не началась работа по новому «Фобосу». Мы сейчас все силы бросаем на проект «ЭкзоМарс»" ("No, work on the new Phobos has not begun. We are throwing all our forces at the ExoMars project right now"). He added that experience from the lunar programme was needed first and that the lessons of the Phobos-Grunt launch had to be absorbed.

facts.label: The technical assignment, 2016
facts.value: The clearest description of Boomerang comes from the technical assignment for the advance project, published on the Russian state procurement site and reported by TASS on 25 October 2016. A 6.5 tonne spacecraft would reach Mars, enter orbits around Mars, Phobos and Deimos and study them remotely, soft-land on Phobos and take samples, and send a return vehicle back to land on Russian territory. The document specified that the descent vehicle's sample container "должен обеспечивать размещение не менее 100 кубических сантиметров вещества Фобоса массой не менее 0,6 кг", at least 100 cubic centimetres of Phobos material weighing at least 0.6 kg. TASS added that the 2011 Phobos-Grunt had been meant to return 100 grams, the low end of the 100 to 200 gram range usually quoted for that mission.

facts.label: Launcher and ground segment
facts.value: The same 2016 assignment named an Angara from the Vostochny cosmodrome. Phobos-Grunt had flown on a Zenit from Baikonur. Control in flight was to use the antennas at Yevpatoria, Kalyazin and Ussuriysk and the deep space communications centre at Medvezhi Ozera, together with ground stations of the European Space Agency. Russian Wikipedia's infobox instead lists Proton-M or Angara-A5 and gives the launch site as unknown.

facts.label: The money
facts.value: The estimate climbed and the work did not. Russian Wikipedia records roughly 3 billion roubles in 2012, 5.1 billion in the 2014 draft programme, and 10.3 billion in the draft Federal Space Programme for 2016 to 2025. The approved programme carried 10,151 million roubles for Phobos research. Separately, Roscosmos was prepared to spend 150.316 million roubles on the advance project alone. None of these figures is a spend; they are allocations and ceilings in successive documents.

facts.label: The European condition
facts.value: The Federal Space Programme's own footnote said the Phobos work would be carried out only with the participation of the European Space Agency. TASS reported that condition twice, on 11 and 25 October 2016. Zelyony described Boomerang as the logical continuation of ExoMars 2016 and ExoMars 2020, contingent on how the ExoMars work went. In 2022 ESA ended its ExoMars cooperation with Roscosmos, which removed the only partner the programme's own paperwork allowed for. Our Kazachok entry covers that decision and its dates.

facts.label: Five launch dates
facts.value: January 2012: not before 2018. May 2015: the draft Federal Space Programme set 2024 for the Expedition-M launch. 5 and 11 October 2016: Zelyony confirmed 2024 and denied press reports of a slip to 2025. 15 July 2017: Zelyony said that because of funding cuts the mission would launch only after 2025. 2 September 2023: TASS, citing NPO Lavochkin materials, said after 2030. Each of those is a statement about a future that then moved again.

facts.label: How far it actually got
facts.value: The tender for the work was run in 2016 and won by NPO Lavochkin, and in 2019 the Phobos expedition passed its first stage: the submission of technical proposals. Zakharov described that as the very first stage of work, the one that comes before preliminary design. At that stage the science payload composition was provisionally fixed, with instruments expected to be better than the 2011 set, and the ballistic scheme was determined. That is as far as it went. No spacecraft structure, no engineering model and no flight hardware were ever built.

facts.label: Why it stopped
facts.value: Zakharov told N+1 in February 2020 that, on his information, a Roscosmos representative had said at a meeting at NPO Lavochkin that there would be no continuation of the work in 2020 because there was no funding, and that further work had been deferred by four years, to 2024, with no development expected in the meantime. He added that the Roscosmos leadership had not announced this publicly. This is the closest thing to a stated cause of death that the project has, and it is a second-hand account of a meeting rather than a decision document.

facts.label: Mars-Grunt, the second half
facts.value: Mars-Grunt was the Mars surface sample return that Expedition-M was ultimately for. It was proposed to Roscosmos by IKI, with NPO Lavochkin as manufacturer, and never advanced beyond planning. English Wikipedia describes a cruise stage derived from Fregat-M, a lander using an inflatable braking cone and retro-rockets rather than parachutes, a robotic arm collecting about 0.2 kg, and a Mars ascent vehicle rendezvousing with an orbiter in a 500 km circular orbit, launched by Angara A5 from Vostochny. Russian Wikipedia describes controlled aerodynamic braking on the same grounds, that parachutes work poorly in the thin Martian atmosphere.

facts.label: Mars-Grunt's numbers do not agree
facts.value: The two published descriptions are not compatible. Russian Wikipedia gives a launch mass of 5,200 kg with a 752 kg landing platform and an ascent rocket of about 1,700 kg. English Wikipedia gives a launch mass of 4,100 kg, a landing mass of 2,750 kg including a 450 kg ascent vehicle, and a 450 kg orbiter dry mass. A 1,700 kg ascent rocket and a 450 kg ascent vehicle are not the same object. Neither article cites a Lavochkin document we could open, and Russian Wikipedia's article was nominated for deletion in August 2023. Treat every Mars-Grunt number as a design study figure of uncertain vintage.

facts.label: Why Phobos first
facts.value: Zakharov's argument for the ordering is the most useful engineering statement anyone has made about this programme. A Mars sample return and a Phobos sample return share almost all their elements, he said, and the only element Phobos does not exercise is the ascent rocket from the surface of Mars. Going to Phobos first was therefore not a consolation prize but a rehearsal. He also said he was certain a Phobos expedition would eventually happen, because the programme it belongs to includes Mars sample return, which must happen sooner or later. The open question, in his words, was when.

facts.label: Someone else is going
facts.value: JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration is now flying the Phobos sample return that Boomerang was designed to be. MMX launched on 20 October 2026 at 04:41:03 Japan time (19:41:03 UTC on 19 October) on an H3 from Tanegashima, and is to reach Mars about a year later, sample Phobos, and return to Earth in Japanese fiscal 2031. Zakharov's response in 2020 to the Japanese schedule was that the two missions do not duplicate each other, and that he had hoped the first Phobos sample return would be Russian: "у нас такая возможность была, но мы ее упустили" ("we had that chance, and we let it slip").

timeline: Phobos-Grunt, stranded in Earth orbit since 8 November 2011, re-enters the atmosphere. Russia's first interplanetary launch in fifteen years is over, and it remains, in 2026, the last Russian-built spacecraft launched toward another planet.

Within nine days of the re-entry, NPO Lavochkin and IKI say publicly that they intend to repeat the mission. Khartov: Russia must solve the task of the flight to Mars. Zelyony: the design will be simplified, and none of Phobos-Grunt's four tasks had ever been rehearsed before it flew.
At MAKS-2013 Khartov states that work on the new Phobos mission has not begun, because everything is going into ExoMars and because the lunar programme has to come first.

TASS reports that the draft Federal Space Programme for 2016 to 2025 sets the launch of the development work Экспедиция-М (Марс-Грунт) for 2024, with 10.3 billion roubles across the decade, double the 5.1 billion in the previous year's draft, which had assumed 2025.

Two weeks after Lev Zelyony tells TASS the launch has not been postponed and remains 2024, the technical assignment for the advance project appears on the state procurement site: a 6.5 tonne spacecraft, an Angara from Vostochny, orbits of Mars, Phobos and Deimos, a soft landing, and a container able to hold at least 100 cubic centimetres and 0.6 kg of Phobos. Roscosmos is ready to spend 150.316 million roubles on the advance project. The programme carries 10,151 million roubles for Phobos research, with a footnote that the work will happen only with European participation.
Zelyony says that because of reduced funding the mission will launch only after 2025, which puts it outside the Federal Space Programme that was paying for it.

The Phobos expedition passes the stage of submitting technical proposals, the first step before preliminary design. A provisional instrument set and a ballistic scheme exist on paper. This is the high-water mark of the whole programme.

Alexander Zakharov of IKI tells N+1 that a Roscosmos representative said at a meeting at NPO Lavochkin that there will be no continuation of the work in 2020 for lack of funding, and that it is deferred four years to 2024. Roscosmos never announces this.

Soon after the start of Russia's military operation in Ukraine, RBC records, the European side refused further cooperation and ESA turned to the United States. Roscosmos called that a threat to Mars exploration, and its head Yuri Borisov asked who would gain from it, Russia or the Europeans, and answered that everyone would lose. The Federal Space Programme footnote had made European participation a condition of the Phobos work.

TASS, citing NPO Lavochkin materials, reports that Boomerang will be launched after 2030. RBC repeats the mission profile unchanged from 2016: 6.5 tonnes, Angara, Vostochny, a return capsule landing in Russia. This is the last schedule statement we could find.

In Troitsky Variant, space analyst Alexander Khokhlov says of Russia's ten-year national space project: "У нас в нацпроекте на десять лет вперед, до 2036 года, нет никакого упоминания Марса, никаких марсианских проектов" ("In our national project ten years ahead, to 2036, there is no mention of Mars, no Martian projects at all").

Rossiyskaya Gazeta reports a draft presidential decree on state policy in space activity, prepared by Roscosmos and published on the federal portal for draft legal acts. Its concentration of resources to 2036 lists the Moon, a lunar nuclear power plant, an orbital station, launchers, constellations and GLONASS. After 2036 it lists Venus, nuclear propulsion and lunar and asteroid resources. Mars appears nowhere.

images.caption: NPO Lavochkin's own computer rendering of the Boomerang spacecraft, published on its project page for КА «Бумеранг», ОКР «Экспедиция-М»: a transfer and landing platform on four legs with dished footpads, four solar wings, gold-blanketed spherical tanks and the return stack on top. The same page lists the launch as after 2030, the launcher as Angara-A5 and the mass as 5000 kg.

A Lavochkin exploded diagram of Phobos-Grunt, the 2011 spacecraft, labelled in Russian from the top down: спускаемый аппарат (the Earth entry capsule), возвращаемый аппарат (the return vehicle), перелетный модуль (the cruise and landing module), переходная ферма (the transfer truss), китайский микроспутник (the Chinese microsatellite Yinghuo-1), маршевая двигательная установка (the main propulsion unit) and сбрасываемый блок баков (the jettisonable tank block). Every part of it is drawn.

A Phobos-Grunt vehicle standing on its landing legs and dished footpads in an assembly hall at the Lavochkin plant, large spherical propellant tanks and instrument boxes exposed, a stowed panel above and handling equipment around it. The Lavochkin gallery publishes the frame with no caption and no date, so whether this is the flight article or a test article is not established.
